findings.issue: `SpinDensityC.deltaQ` (line 128) and `SpinDensityC.transversity` (line 133) name the same leading-twist quantities that the adjacent real API in the same `PDF` namespace calls `g1` and `h1` (`Positivity.lean:134`, `:139`), so one namespace carries two vocabularies for one quantity. The split is visible inside the file itself: `g1_re : PDF.g1 ρ.re = ρ.deltaQ` (line 168), `h1_re : PDF.h1 ρ.re = ρ.transversity.re` (line 173), and `SpinDensity.deltaQ_toSpinDensityC : ρ.toSpinDensityC.deltaQ = PDF.g1 ρ` (line 355). A `g1`/`h1` grep misses the complex API entirely.

findings.evidence: PosSemidef.lean:123-124 statement coerces both vectors; PosSemidef.lean:142-143 `re (star x ⬝ᵥ (M.map ((↑) : ℝ → 𝕜) *ᵥ x))` with `x : n → 𝕜` uses the same bare `star` token.
findings.fix: Rename to `Matrix.re_star_ofReal_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal`, and update the `## Main results` entry (line 55) and the reference in `PosSemidef.map_re`'s docstring (line 132).
findings.issue: `Matrix.re_star_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal` places `ofReal` only after `mulVec`, but in the statement both vectors are coerced: `re (star (fun i => (x i : 𝕜)) ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ fun i => (x i : 𝕜)))`. The sibling `re_star_dotProduct_map_ofReal_mulVec` (line 142) uses a bare `star` for a genuinely 𝕜-valued vector, so `star` without qualifier already means something else in this section — the name reads as if only the right-hand vector were real.

summary: Two naming issues in the reviewed head: the complex API uses a second vocabulary (`deltaQ`/`transversity`) for the quantities the adjacent real API calls `g1`/`h1`, and `re_star_dotProduct_mulVec_ofReal` misdescribes which argument is coerced. Namespacing, suffix strength, and the absence of notation are fine.
